nodes.description: Male mice homozygous for a CRISPR-induced frameshift in Cfap65 have sperm phenotypes consistent with human MMAF.

Knockout males have severe MMAF, acrosome and manchette defects and reduced sperm counts; females remain fertile. Respiratory cilia lose the C2a projection without overt disease, and on a pure C57BL/6 background over two-thirds of pups develop hydrocephalus, most dying before three weeks of age.
Coiled flagella are part of the MMAF mosaic.

nodes.description: ICSI is the only route to biological parenthood, and patient sperm can fertilize oocytes, but outcomes have been poor: three couples underwent two cycles each with fertilization rates of 22-69% and only biochemical pregnancies that miscarried, and ICSI outcomes for two further patients were also unfavorable. Head defects, acrosome hypoplasia and impaired nuclear condensation are the proposed reasons. Assisted oocyte activation and other strategies have been suggested but not reported.
